partial_case.facts: The resident has lived at a 1-bedroom semi-detached bungalow since 2019. The landlord's records say the resident is elderly and she suffers from breathing problems. The resident has experienced problems with damp and mould at the property and first raised concerns to the landlord in 2020. The resident reported damp and mould in her property several times from January 2020 to November 2024. The landlord attended and carried out mould treatment and some repairs. On 28 February 2025, the resident complained to the landlord that it had not treated the cause of damp and mould in the property despite her reporting it for several years. On 3 April 2025, the landlord sent its stage 1 complaint response apologising and offering £250 for the delay in carrying out inspections and repairs. The resident escalated her complaint as she was not happy with its response. On 9 May 2025, the landlord sent its stage 2 complaint response offering a further £100 compensation as it had not explained what action it would take following her initial complaint.

partial_case.facts: The landlord is Barnsley Metropolitan Borough Council, a local authority landlord. The resident has a secure tenancy and has lived in a 1-bedroom semi-detached bungalow since 2019. The landlord’s records say the resident is elderly and has breathing problems. The resident experienced damp and mould and first raised concerns to the landlord in 2020. The complaint concerned the landlord’s handling of reports of damp and mould and the associated complaint. From January 2020 to November 2024 the resident reported damp and mould several times and the landlord attended, carried out mould treatment and some repairs. On 28 February 2025 the resident complained that the landlord had not treated the cause despite reports over several years. The landlord sent stage 1 and stage 2 complaint responses in April and May 2025, apologising and offering compensation.

findings: Severe maladministration in how the landlord handled reports of damp and mould in the property.
No maladministration in the landlord’s complaint handling.
orders: Payment of £1,500 compensation to the resident, with the £350 offered during the internal complaints process deductible if already paid.
Inspection and schedule of works for outstanding repairs.

key_reasoning_quotes.text: Despite numerous reports of damp and mould in the resident’s property, the landlord failed address the root cause of the problem over a prolonged period.
there is no evidence the landlord conducted works or inspections which sought to determine the cause of the damp and mould in the property.

The landlord has not provided evidence which explained why there was a gap and inactivity between the resident’s report on 12 April 2024 and its inspection on 18 June 2024. This was not in accordance with its damp and mould policy.
There is clear evidence of repeated visits to conduct works at the property, which have failed to tackle the root cause of the issue.

The failure to effectively deal with the damp and mould at the property over a 5 year period, together with the failure to provide appropriate redress to this point, leads to a determination of severe maladministration
